accounting.rationale: PDF 79, printed 65, lines 2-3 introduces polymorphic entities and the possibility of differing dynamic types, not a mandate that every instance changes type.
CLASS is the polymorphic declaration route. R703 and C705/C708 remain the syntax, extensibility and eligible-entity owners.

A polymorphic data entity can have differing dynamic types during execution. The actual state-dependent rules are executable requirements below; type parameters and rank are not synonymous with dynamic type.
PDF 79 lines 4-9: declaration-order restriction and qualified function-prefix interpretation, not only terminology.
PDF 79 line 10 defines the declared type for a named CLASS specifier, independently of the current dynamic type; p5 and the ancestor-part witness preserve this distinction.
The definition applies when the CLASS specifier contains a type name, not to CLASS(*).
That specified type is the declared type even if the object is allocated/associated with an extension. Neither SAME_TYPE_AS nor EXTENDS_TYPE_OF queries a general declared-type relation.
PDF 79 lines 11-13 defines CLASS(*) and the absence of a same-declared-type relation; canonical compatibility uses are accounted in 7.3.3.
CLASS(*) is unlimited polymorphic. It is not assumed-type TYPE(*), which has additional C714-C716 restrictions.
An unlimited polymorphic declaration does not specify a declared type. An intrinsic current dynamic type does not create one.
No entity, including another unlimited polymorphic entity, shares a declared type with it. Being compatible with all entities is a different relation.
PDF 79 lines 14-19 supplies six state/association-dependent semantic rules, with the inactive-state sentence split into its two cases.

requirements.title: Named CLASS declarations require a previously defined derived type
requirements.definition: The derived type in a named CLASS type declaration must already be defined. For a function result, the FUNCTION statement may specify a type defined within that function or accessible there by use or host association. CLASS(*) is outside this named-type premise. Extensibility and dummy/allocatable/pointer eligibility remain separately required.

pending.ordering-source-use: Needs a source-bound canonical declaration-order and accessibility join with a minimal exclusion/control pair under its actual numbered or Clause 19 reporting owner. The two allowed-prefix controls do not test exclusion. No fatal-rejection expectation is inferred merely from p2's shall, and body-local result interpretation is authored separately.

requirements.oracle: Two positive controls return allocated initialized CLASS results with a type defined earlier in the host or imported only inside the function. The use-only control renames the type in the caller so its prefix cannot succeed merely through that host spelling.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Every named CLASS type is extensible and every result is ALLOCATABLE. Allocation is checked before data use. Neither control relies on TYPEOF/CLASSOF or redeclares the result type after specifying it in the prefix.

requirements.title: A function-prefix CLASS result follows its body-local derived type
requirements.definition: A CLASS result whose FUNCTION prefix names a derived type defined inside the function is interpreted as declared immediately after that definition. The result remains polymorphic; its ALLOCATABLE or POINTER attribute must be specified as required for a nondummy CLASS entity and must not redundantly restate the result type.
requirements.oracle: The function defines a local root and extension, gives its prefix-declared result ALLOCATABLE, allocates the extension and checks initialized components in a TYPE IS branch. It sets a checked output sentinel from the result and returns it through a SOURCE allocation of CLASS(*); the caller checks allocation and rank. The local type is not moved to the host to appease an implementation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The caller cannot name the function-local type, so its allocation/rank observations are not an independent named-type identity test. The function's actual branch and component checks supply the local result oracle. The output sentinel starts negative, preventing a skipped function body from passing. No unsupported result is converted to an empty compile control.
requirements.dependencies: C705/C708; 7.5.7.1 (PDF 104); 9.7.1.1/C937/C950-C951 (PDF 160-161); 11.1.11.2 (PDF 225-226); 15.6.2.2 p3-p4 (PDF 354). The ordinary OUT sentinel is not an assumed-type or polymorphic dummy.

requirements.title: An allocated polymorphic allocatable has its allocation's type
requirements.definition: While an allocatable polymorphic object is allocated, its dynamic type is the type established by its allocation. The declared type of named CLASS does not become that extension. Unlimited polymorphic allocation can establish an intrinsic dynamic type. Allocation eligibility, parameter agreement, rank and SOURCE/MOLD rules are separate premises.
requirements.oracle: Four effect programs distinguish root and multilevel-extension allocations, SOURCE allocation from an already allocated polymorphic extension, separate default/double REAL allocations, and CHARACTER allocations of different lengths. SELECT TYPE includes failing defaults and checks initialized payloads; length is checked separately from type and kind.
requirements.oracle_limitation: STAT and ALLOCATED checks precede each object inquiry or access. Explicitly allocated payloads are initialized before reads; SOURCE payloads are already defined. Default/double kinds come from KIND literals, not storage sizes, and their mandated precision distinction is not generalized to arbitrary kind numbers. TYPE IS tests type plus kind, not LEN or a universal compatibility relation.

requirements.title: An associated polymorphic pointer takes its target's dynamic type
requirements.definition: An associated polymorphic pointer has the dynamic type of its target, not necessarily the target's declared type. Reassociation to a different eligible target can change that dynamic type. This rule presupposes a live target and defined associated pointer status; it does not authorize access after target deallocation or a forbidden type/kind/rank association.
requirements.oracle: Three programs associate with initialized sibling extension targets, with an allocated polymorphic target whose dynamic type differs from its declared root, and with fixed-length character targets through CLASS(*). Each checks ASSOCIATED before SELECT TYPE or length/value inquiry, with explicit failing defaults.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Pointers are initialized to NULL and nullified before a target is deallocated. No target is reallocated while an alias is used. Character kind and length are not taken as type identity, and no intrinsic argument restriction is bypassed by SAME_TYPE_AS.

requirements.title: An ordinary polymorphic dummy takes its effective argument's dynamic type
requirements.definition: A polymorphic dummy without ALLOCATABLE and without POINTER has its effective argument's dynamic type. A pointer actual can supply its target as that effective argument. The dummy's own rank and parameter declarations and the argument-association restrictions still apply; this is not the rule for allocatable or pointer dummies.
requirements.oracle: Three effect programs pass a concrete extension and an allocated CLASS(root) extension to the same ordinary CLASS(root) dummy, pass a guarded associated pointer actual, and pass initialized REAL and CHARACTER actuals to CLASS(*). TYPE IS branches set checked result tags and examine defined components or values.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Actual allocation/association is checked at the call sites; the ordinary dummies themselves have neither attribute. No absent OPTIONAL actual is queried, no TYPE(*) actual is illegally passed to CLASS(*), and the exact-kind and assumed-length guards satisfy C1165. Tags distinguish missing dispatch from successful zero-initialization.

requirements.title: Inactive objects with a declared type have that dynamic type
requirements.definition: An unallocated allocatable object or a disassociated pointer has its declared type as its dynamic type. Undefined pointer association is not disassociation. CLASS(*) has no declared type, so this sentence supplies no invented concrete type for an inactive unlimited entity.
requirements.oracle: Three programs first establish the expected inactive state using ALLOCATED or ASSOCIATED, then use SAME_TYPE_AS only with extensible declared types and initialized extensible molds. Allocatable and pointer witnesses are also observed while active with a different dynamic type and then after DEALLOCATE or NULLIFY. A nonpolymorphic inactive control covers the sentence's broader object scope.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The intrinsic explicitly permits these objects when polymorphic pointer status is defined. It does not read components, deferred parameters or elements of inactive objects. At least one extensible dynamic type makes the equality result determinate. No such equality is asserted for two inactive CLASS(*) objects, and EXTENDS_TYPE_OF's special unlimited cases are not reinterpreted as general compatibility.
requirements.dependencies: 7.3.2.3 p3-p4; 9.7.3 and pointer association status in 19.5.2; 16.1 p2's explicit inactive/undefined-value inquiry permission (PDF 364); 16.9.177 p3/p5 and NOTE 1 (PDF 452), contrasted with 16.9.86 (PDF 409). These inquiry clauses are dependencies, not owned intrinsic test coverage.

requirements.title: An associate-name entity has its selector's dynamic type
requirements.definition: The entity identified by an associate name has the dynamic type of the selector with which it is associated. Declared type, polymorphism and other attributes are governed by the defining construct. In particular an ASSOCIATE name does not simply inherit its selector's ALLOCATABLE or POINTER attribute.
requirements.oracle: Four programs associate names with an allocated polymorphic array, an associated polymorphic pointer, an allocated unlimited character object, and a nonpolymorphic derived constructor expression. Exact branch/type checks and initialized payload checks are made inside the association. The array's size is checked before element access, and its rank is distinguished from type.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Dynamic selector state is guarded before entering ASSOCIATE. The associate name is never queried with ALLOCATED or ASSOCIATED merely because the selector has that attribute. The expression selector is read only, and no selector is deallocated, nullified or absent while associated.
requirements.dependencies: 11.1.3.1-.3 (PDF 204-205), especially declared type, polymorphism, rank and absent-OPTIONAL premises; 11.1.11.2 p3-p8 (PDF 225-226); 19.5.1.6. No coarray/CHANGE TEAM execution is claimed.

requirements.title: A nonpolymorphic object's dynamic type is its declared type
requirements.definition: For a nonpolymorphic object, dynamic type is its declared type. Type parameters and rank remain distinct attributes. Associating a nonpolymorphic pointer with the declared-type part of a polymorphic target does not make that pointer's dynamic type the target's extension.

pending.nonextensible-source-use: Needs a bounded canonical source-use join for SEQUENCE, BIND(C), the excluded intrinsic-module pointer types, enum and enumeration objects. SAME_TYPE_AS on an ordinary nonextensible object violates its argument premise; two unlimited nonextensible dynamic types can have a processor-dependent result, and SELECT TYPE excludes BIND/SEQUENCE guards. Do not invent an intrinsic oracle or equate C descriptors/storage sizes with named type identity. The extensible and intrinsic witnesses here do not close this graph.

requirements.oracle: Three programs inspect initialized intrinsic actuals through eligible CLASS(*) dummies, distinguish two same-shaped but separately defined extensible types with SAME_TYPE_AS, and associate a TYPE(root) pointer with a CLASS(root) target allocated as an extension. The last case verifies root identity and inherited-component aliasing while preserving an extension-component sentinel.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The derived molds have extensible declared and dynamic types, so the equality inquiry has a defined result; no claim about kind, length or compatibility follows from it. The ancestor association is permitted because the pointer and target have the same declared root, with no differing kind or rank. The extended payload is initialized before the root alias is formed and checked before the target dies.

review_rationale: Independent source/link review and verified integration: doc/source_audits/batch_008.json. Declared versus dynamic type and the allocation, pointer, argument, selector and nonpolymorphic cases preserve their canonical premises, initialized values and lifetime/allocation guards. Nonextensible identity and declaration-order graphs remain explicit gaps.
